feature: Run 1 — golden-vector conformance harness + progressive-loan schedule-generator PoC port
requirement: Prove the Fineract→Go migration pipeline end-to-end on the smallest real slice, harness-first. IN SCOPE for THIS run only: (1) Build the golden-vector conformance harness (.softhouse/conformance.sh) and a vector store, capturing vectors for the progressive-loan schedule generator from the live Fineract oracle. (2) Define the minimal frozen adapter interface needed to invoke a schedule generator (spec_writer) — mark its ratification a user gate. (3) Port fineract-progressive-loan-embeddable-schedule-generator (~182 LOC) to Go behind that interface (coder), integer-minor-units only, no float in any path. (4) Verify via /softhouse-uat: go build + the schedule-generator conformance vectors must pass, and property invariants (schedule principal amortizes to exactly zero, rounding matches Fineract) must hold. Every coder/analyst task gets a paired INDEPENDENT reviewer that RE-DERIVES the schedule arithmetic against the Fineract vector, not reads it. SCOPE GUARD: Minimum Portable Core, PoC slice only — do NOT plan GL posting logic, COB, charges/rates/tax, provisioning, or ANY context cutover in this run; record them to backlog in strangler order (GL → loan lifecycle → charges/rates/tax → COB → provisioning). Route as user gates: adapter-contract ratification and any cutover. This run also exercises the token-limit checkpoint/resume once.
backlog: Run 2 — General Ledger / accounting (double-entry posting rules, chart of accounts, journal entries/items) behind the frozen contract; GL vectors + trial-balance invariants. Cutover = separate user gate.

Run 3 — Loan product + schedule + lifecycle (products, interest methods, disbursement, repayment, penalties, rescheduling, write-off), reusing the Run 1 schedule generator. Cutover = separate user gate.
Run 4 — Charges / rates / tax including the VAT / e-Barimt tie-in; thresholds from config. Cutover = separate user gate.
Run 5 — Close-of-business batch (daily accrual/aging/posting, idempotency, restart-after-failure) on Nexus's scheduler, EOD day-over-day parity. Cutover = separate user gate.

Run 6 — Provisioning + FRC reporting feeds (Tier-A completion); compliance-spine capital and 30%/70% limits reconcile to the native GL. Tier-A cutover + regulatory acceptance = user gates, parallel run required.

tasks.title: Stand up + pin the Fineract reference oracle (on PostgreSQL)
tasks.description: Bring up the Fineract reference oracle reachable for this run and pin it: exact release tag/commit, JVM version, tenant/loan-product seed data, and the local source checkout path for fineract-progressive-loan-embeddable-schedule-generator. DATABASE IS POSTGRESQL, mandatory: start it with the postgresql compose profile (docker-compose-postgresql.yml / config/docker/compose/postgresql.yml) — never the mysql or mariadb compose files — and ASSERT the running config before recording it: driverClassName == org.postgresql.Driver, jdbcUrl starts jdbc:postgresql://, and no ojdbc / oracle.jdbc / port 1521 anywhere in the stack. Record all of it in .softhouse/reference-oracle.md (connection facts, Postgres server version, pinned Fineract commit, the driver assertion result) so every later vector capture is reproducible against the SAME oracle build on the SAME engine. Terminology: 'oracle' here means the Fineract reference implementation; Oracle Database is prohibited by CLAUDE.md. If the reference oracle cannot be brought up, STOP the run here — conformance must never report a false PASS (exit 2 on unreachable).
tasks.note: DONE 2026-08-17 local fire. Oracle UP on PostgreSQL 18.3; Fineract commit 426a23544 (== pinned commit of record), JVM Zulu 21.0.11. Driver assertions passed against the RUNNING container: org.postgresql.Driver + jdbc:postgresql://. Prohibited engines: 0 ojdbc/oracle.jdbc/mysql/mariadb entries in the jar, no :1521 listener. Host had no JVM/brew, so the image is built from the pinned checkout inside eclipse-temurin:21-jdk via .softhouse/bin/build-oracle-image.sh. Facts in .softhouse/reference-oracle.md.

tasks.title: Draft DEC-1: minimal frozen adapter interface for schedule generation
tasks.description: Write docs/adr/DEC-1-schedule-generator-adapter.md plus the Go interface stub it ratifies (nexus/internal/apps/loanschedule/contract/contract.go): the SMALLEST boundary that lets either Fineract-JVM or the Go module answer 'generate a repayment schedule'. Money strictly int64 minor units (MNT, ISO 4217 numeric 496, minor unit 2) in every request/response field; rates as basis points or explicit rational, never float; dates as civil dates plus an explicit IANA tz (Asia/Ulaanbaatar | Asia/Hovd, never an offset); deterministic ordering; no Fineract internal types leaking through. Document the switch mechanism (config, per context) and state explicitly that ratification of DEC-1 and ANY later change to it is a user gate. Do not implement the generator here.

tasks.title: Independent review of DEC-1 adapter contract
tasks.description: Adversarial review of DEC-1 and the interface stub: is it minimal (nothing in it that only one implementation needs)? Any float, any decimal-string money, any hard-coded tz offset, any first_name/last_name, any Fineract type leak, any field that would force a contract change once GL and loan lifecycle arrive in Runs 2–3? Re-derive that the response shape can express Fineract's per-period split and final-period balancing WITHOUT loss. Findings must be actionable before ratification.
tasks.note: Contract is the boundary — reviewed before the user gate. | MUST review DEC-1 against the CORRECTED T2 document (attempt 1 was rejected; T4 drafted against the uncorrected version — check specifically that the day-count/rounding policy fields survive the T3 corrections). || ORCHESTRATOR FLAG for the T5 reviewer: DEC-1 defines IntermediatePrecisionDigits as SIGNIFICANT DECIMAL DIGITS, but T3 found Fineract's setScale(mc.getPrecision(),..) feeds precision into the SCALE slot (decimal places), truncating rate factors. Significant-digits vs scale is a possible contract defect that would break bit-exact parity — T5 must settle it against source.

tasks.title: USER GATE — ratify DEC-1 frozen adapter contract
tasks.description: Human decision gate. Buyan ratifies (or amends) DEC-1. Nothing downstream may proceed on an unratified contract, and no agent may change it afterwards — a later change is a new user task. Blocks T7, T8 and T10.

tasks.title: Build the golden-vector conformance harness + vector store
tasks.description: Write .softhouse/conformance.sh and the vector store: .softhouse/vectors/<context>/<case>.json, schema documented in .softhouse/vectors/README.md, keyed to the ratified DEC-1 request/response shape with all money as integer minor-unit strings/ints (never floats in the JSON). conformance.sh: takes an optional context filter, replays every vector through the Go implementation, diffs field-by-field against the captured oracle output, prints a per-vector PASS/FAIL table, exit 0 all-pass / 1 mismatch / 2 harness-or-oracle-unusable (never a false PASS). Also write the Go table-driven conformance test and the property invariants: sum(principal portions) == principal exactly, closing balance == 0 exactly, sum(period splits) == period total, monotonic due dates, no float anywhere (grep guard on the package). Include one hand-authored fixture vector so the harness is testable before capture.
tasks.note: Harness-first: the coder task depends on this.

tasks.title: Capture golden vectors from the live Fineract oracle
tasks.description: Orchestrator task: drive the pinned oracle from T1 to produce the T2/T3-approved config matrix and write the captured request/response pairs into .softhouse/vectors/loan-schedule/ in T7's schema, one file per case, each stamped with the oracle version from .softhouse/reference-oracle.md. Capture the raw oracle output verbatim (full scale/precision as returned) alongside the contract-shaped form so rounding can be re-derived later. No Go implementation exists yet — these are oracle-only captures. If the oracle is unreachable, fail loudly; do not synthesise vectors.
tasks.note: Vector capture is orchestrator-only (touches the oracle).

tasks.title: Independent review of harness + captured vectors (re-derive + mutation check)
tasks.description: Fresh reviewer. (a) Hand re-derive at least three captured vectors — one uneven-division principal, one 0% rate, one month-end/leap-year date — from the Fineract conventions in T2 and confirm the captured numbers, digit for digit; a vector that cannot be re-derived is rejected, not explained. (b) Mutation-test the harness: perturb one rounding step / one period split in a scratch copy and confirm conformance.sh goes RED and that a stopped oracle yields exit 2, not PASS. (c) Confirm no float appears in any vector JSON and that vector coverage matches the approved matrix.
tasks.note: A harness nobody proved can fail is not a harness.

tasks.title: Port the progressive-loan schedule generator to Go behind DEC-1
tasks.description: Implement nexus/internal/apps/loanschedule (generator.go + emi.go + rounding.go) as a faithful port of fineract-progressive-loan-embeddable-schedule-generator behind the ratified DEC-1 interface. int64 minor units only — no float32/float64, no float-backed decimal, not even in intermediates; integer/rational arithmetic with the rounding mode and scale documented in T2 applied at exactly the same points Fineract applies it. Deterministic, no wall-clock reads, tz from the request. Acceptance criteria are the .softhouse/vectors/loan-schedule/ vectors from T8 plus T7's property invariants — the port is done when conformance.sh is green for this context, not when it looks right. If a vector cannot be matched without changing DEC-1, STOP and report: a contract change is a user task.

tasks.title: Independent adversarial review of the Go port (re-derives the arithmetic)
tasks.description: Spawned fresh without planning context. RE-DERIVE the EMI, every period's interest/principal split, and the final-period balancing from the Fineract source conventions and the captured vector inputs — compute independently, then compare to the Go output. Do NOT read the Go code and confirm it looks equivalent; that is the exact failure mode this project has already been burned by. Then HARD checks on the diff: no float type or float-backed decimal anywhere; no balance written directly; no hard-coded tz offset or hard-coded MNT 5,000,000-class threshold; no first_name/last_name; no member-savings insured/protected/guaranteed string; no wall-clock or locale dependence. Verdict APPROVED / MICRO-FIX / REJECTED with the re-derived numbers shown.
tasks.note: Paired independent reviewer for T10 — mandatory, re-derives.

tasks.title: Token-limit checkpoint / resume drill (exercise once)
tasks.description: Deliberately exercise the scheduler path once in this run: at a chosen point after T10 starts, signal the active worker(s) to checkpoint (commit WIP to branch, write .softhouse/state/<squad>.STATE.json with current item/step/next action), write .softhouse/RESUME.md, then resume via /softhouse resume and confirm the run rehydrates at the earliest incomplete dependency level WITHOUT re-executing completed tasks or re-capturing vectors. Record the drill outcome (what resumed cleanly, what had to be redone) for the postmortem.
tasks.note: Required by the run requirement; orchestrator-only.

tasks.title: Verify: /softhouse-uat — build, tests, conformance, invariants

Report the per-vector table verbatim. A PASS here means 'builds, tests green, known-bad patterns absent, matches the oracle on captured vectors' — explicitly NOT 'safe to cut over'.
tasks.note: Run gate — must PASS before the run completes.

Cutover of the schedule/loan context remains a separate user gate requiring vectors passing + a clean shadow-parity window + regulatory / parallel-run sign-off.
